name: Shephatiah
overview: The name Shephatiah appears in Scripture associated with several individuals who played distinct roles in Israel's history. Notably, Shephatiah was a son of David through Abital, indicating his royal lineage (2 Samuel 3:4; 1 Chronicles 3:3). Another Shephatiah was a Benjamite and father of Meshullam, reflecting family lines important in post-exilic restoration (1 Chronicles 9:8). Additionally, a valiant Shephatiah joined David at Ziklag, and one served as a ruler over the tribe of Simeon, showing leadership within Israel's tribal structure (1 Chronicles 12:5; 27:16). The presence of Shephatiah as a son of Jehoshaphat further ties the name to the Davidic dynasty and governance (2 Chronicles 21:2). These references collectively reveal Shephatiah as a name linked to faithful service, leadership, and covenantal heritage within God's unfolding redemptive plan.
